title: Understanding SVD
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), a matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values on its diagonal, which represent the magnitude of the principal components.

title: Role of Matrix U
text: The matrix U in SVD contains the left singular vectors. Each column of U corresponds to a principal component, and the first column represents the direction of the first principal component.

title: Using U to Compute Latent Features
